MURDER IN PRISON - the death of Quintin Fortuin

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight we unravel what really happened to a 39-year old awaiting trial prisoner at Goodwood Prison in the Cape

Unique Selling Point:
We are able to tell the story of the murder of Quinton Fortuin in Goodwood Prison on the 16th of February 2025, because we have been leaked so much information about it: photographs of the dead body, phone calls, the post mortem, an initial inquiry by the Judicial Inspectorate and the answers to Parliamentary questions on the matter. None of this information squares up to the official version disseminated by the Department of Correctional Services of the death of this notorious inmate who grew up in gang-ridden Delft, and who has been in the crosshairs of the judicial system for his entire adult life.

Summary:
On the 16th of February, an awaiting trial prisoner at Goodwood Prison failed to emerge immediately out of his cell when called for roll call. According to insiders, he had been doing drugs all night and was slow to react when the other prisoners were called to come outside to kneel down to be counted.

He was chivvied by the two warders on duty, who got him to join the tail end of the group. But then an altercation ensued. According to Correctional Services, this prisoner, allegedly a senior general in the 26 gang, produced a home-made sharp object and stabbed a warder. In the scuffle the two warders were injured, one broke his arm, and both are home still recuperating over six weeks later. As for the prisoner, Quinton Fortuin, he ended up naked and fatally injured, and was declared dead in Karl Bremer Hospital four and a half hours later.

What happened between about 08h00 in the morning and 11h30 that day when he was declared dead is now contested. It is alleged that Inmate Fortuin was beaten up by wardens who set dogs on him, and then by the EST, the Emergency Security Team that enforces law and order inside the prison walls. It is also alleged that he was dead on the scene and the Department of Correctional Services is desperately trying to cover it up, pretending he died in hospital.

They unnatural death - now a criminal investigation into murder - shows how the prison system fails itself, its inmates and the community at large. It raises the problems of understaffing at prisons, the over population of prisons, the lack of humane control, the lack of any type of rehabilitation or leadership and the lack of technological resources. It's been revealed that none of this was captured on camera because the contract to keep the cameras had not been paid in three years, so while the camera could provide images in real time, it could not record.


Further information:
The story has been in the media, as was the press conference on May the first, but I think there is more to dig in here, than has been reported, and the disconnect between the narratives reveal a serious attempt to cover up the kind of violence which may becoming the norm, in order to keep over crowded, understaffed prisons under control.

Press Release:


Death Behind Bars
In an overcrowded Cape Town prison, an awaiting-trial inmate lies naked, severely beaten. Hours later, he’s declared dead. The official report: the alleged gangster died in a prison fight. But leaked information suggests the story may be far more sinister. What really happened that day? From horrific photos to reports of broken security cameras and attack dogs… whispers swirl, and more questions are raised than answers. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Lourensa Eckard

Script:


MURDER IN PRISON – the death of Quintin Fortuin
Final Script

(VO1) IN CAPE TOWN AN AWAITING-TRIAL PRISONER CHARGED WITH MURDER DIES A PAINFUL DEATH….

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
I think the undertaker had gone about three or four times to collect the body. There was always issues with the paperwork.

(VO2) THE WOUNDS ON HIS BODY PRESENT EVIDENCE OF A VIOLENT BEATING…

Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Hy kom van ‘n moeder af, hy’s sy ma se kind, om iemand so wreed dood te maak, dis nie reg nie.
He was born of a mother - he’s his mother’s child.
To kill somebody so violently is not right.

(VO3) AND THE STORY TOLD BY THE PRISON AUTHORITIES SIMPLY DOESN’T ADD UP.

Singabakho Nxumalo
Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services
Yes, he was disarmed and force was used. Hence, then he needed medical attention.

(VO4) 39-YEAR-OLD QUINTIN FORTUIN WAS THE THIRD INMATE TO DIE CONTROVERSIALLY IN SOUTH AFRICAN PRISONS THIS YEAR.
THESE DEATHS ARE TEARING OPEN THE VEIL OF SECRECY BEHIND WHICH PRISON OFFICIALS DO THEIR JOBS, ALBEIT UNDER VERY DIFFICULT CIRCUMSTANCES.

This is Goodwood Prison in Cape Town.
It’s seriously under-staffed - and dangerously over-crowded.
On the 16th of February this year, only 95 officials were on duty to manage 2400 prisoners.
It was a Sunday morning, and around 08h00 am, we are told, a fight broke out between three warders and a prisoner, a known gangster.

(VO5)THE GANGSTER WAS QUINTIN “QUESTION” FORTUIN A HIGH-RANKING MEMBER OF A PRISON GANG…A GENERAL IN THE 26S.
HE REPORTEDLY REFUSED TO COME OUT FROM HIS CELL TO BE COUNTED AND THEN, WE ARE TOLD, UNPROVOKED, HE STABBED A WARDER.

(VO6) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES SPOKESPERSON SINGABAKHO NXUMALO SAID THREE OFFICIALS BATTLED TO RESTRAIN THE INMATE WHO WEIGHED ONLY 60 KG.

Singabakho Nxumalo
Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services
The official was badly stabbed. In trying to defend himself, he even fell and broke his arm. Another official tried also to assist. He also got injured. Other officials realized that we needed more manpower here, and then, I think they managed then to defuse the situation. But in that act, force was used. The incident happened at about 10 past eight in the morning. He was then taken to Karl Bremer hospital and he passed on just after twelve midday. That is when we received a call that he had passed on.

It takes about fifteen minutes to drive from Goodwood Prison to Karl Bremer Hospital within the speed limit, on a Sunday.
The post mortem says Quintin Fortuin was delivered to the hospital just before 11h00 am.
So what happened in the hours before that?

(VO7) THE PRISONS SPOKESPERSON SAYS THE SITUATION WAS TOO “DYNAMIC” TO PROVIDE A DETAILED TIME-BOUND BREAKDOWN OF THE SEQUENCE OF EVENTS.

Singabakho Nxumalo: It's not just a matter of saying that you slapped me, I slapped you, and that's the end of the story.

Lourensa Eckard: Well, we have a body.

Singabakho Nxumalo: Yes.

Lourensa Eckard: Someone died.

Siyabakho Nxumalo: Yes, and there is a number of people in that particular space. Let's allow that process to take time, otherwise it will not do us any good in saying, let's rush, rush.

(VO7b)BUT FORTUIN’S LAWYER, LABIEK SAMUELS, WANTED TO FIND OUT.
AFTER MAKING OVER A HUNDRED PHONE CALLS TO THE PRISON, HE LOCATED HIS CLIENT AT A MORTUARY.
AND ACCOMPANIED HIS MOTHER TO IDENTIFY HER SON, THROUGH A SMALL WINDOW.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
When we came to the mortuary, the body was placed in such a position that one could not see any of the injuries sustained.ut you could see that his jaw was dislocated and his eyes were still open. His mother then entered the room, and she collapsed.

(VO8) FORTUIN’S MOTHER, MARIA, IS STILL IN A STATE OF DISBELIEF.

Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Hy’t gelê daar.
He lay there;
Sy mond was wa-wyd oop.
his mouth was wide open,
Sy kop was so effens oop, en krappe in sy gesig.
his eye was slightly open, and he had scratches on his face.

(VO9) BUT MARIA SAYS THAT AT THE MORTUARY SHE SUSPECTED THERE WAS MORE TO HER SON’S DEATH THAN MET THE EYE: HE WAS NAKED EXCEPT FOR BOXER SHORTS AND THIS PIECE OF JEWELLERY.


Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Wat ek gekry daar was net ‘n ring.
What I got there was only a ring.
En ‘n trunkie, dis al.
and boxer shorts - that’s all.
Verder, het ons niks verder gekry nie, Toe vra ek die outjie wat daar werk: So ek vra waar’s die klere?
We received nothing further. It was all that he had on him. So, I asked the guy who worked there, “Where are his clothes?”
Hy sê nee hy kom van Karl Bremer af net met ‘n trunkie aan.
He said, no, he came from Karl Bremer Hospital in only his underwear.

(VO10) SO THEY TRACKED BACK TO KARL BREMER HOSPITAL TO FIND HIS CLOTHES AND HOPEFULLY MORE CLUES.

Labiek Samuels: We were also told that he arrived there in that state. Now this exacerbated the entire scenario.

Lourensa Eckard: Did you get the idea that the Correctional Service officials - that they were not completely forthcoming about what had happened?

Labiek Samuels: Most definitely, the version that we were told did not make sense.

(VO11) AT THE TIME, GOODWOOD PRISON TOLD THEM FORTUIN HAD NO POSSESSIONS.
AND THEY OFFERED TO BURY THE BODY THEMSELVES, A CLAIM WHICH CORRECTIONAL SERVICES NOW SAYS IS STRANGE.

Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Hulle wil nie die body van my kind release nie.
They didn’t want to release the body of my child.

Die Vrydag moet die prokureur weer foon vir iemand om te sê release Quintin Fortuin se body en tog release hulle die body vir ons.
That Friday, the lawyer had to phone someone again to say they must release Quintin Fortuin’s body. And only then did they release him to us.

(VO12)HIS BLOODIED BODY WAS FINALLY PREPARED FOR BURIAL BY UNDERTAKER, JP DAVIDS.

JP Davids
Undertaker
Met Quintin jy kon sien daar’s taamlike ‘’n bietjie plekke wat waar hy’t baie seer gekry het.
With Quintin, you could see there were quite a few places where he was very badly hurt.

(VO13) DAVIDS HELPED SAMUELS PHOTOGRAPH THE DEAD MAN’S WOUNDS.
FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE LAWYER SAW BOTH SIDES OF THE CORPSE.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
I saw lacerations of his body. I saw bruises. I saw broken wrist. I saw dog bites and I saw stab wounds.

JP Davids
Undertaker
Daar was natuurlik byt-merke op hom, dit kan ek honderd per sent sê.
There were, of course, also bite marks on him, that I can say for sure
Ons het diep snye op hom gekry en so on, so ja.
We also found deep cuts on his him and so on.

(VO14) DOG BITE MARKS WERE NOT RECORDED ON THE POST MORTEM REPORT.
NOT ALL THE WOUNDS IN THE PHOTOS WERE ACCOUNTED FOR IN THE VERSION OF EVENTS PROVIDED BY THE PRISON.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
There was no sign for me that there was any medical intervention, and that, raised more questions. And from there, I contacted the detective.

PTC: The police are pursuing a charge of murder into the death of Quintin Fortuin.
The eyewitnesses to his unnatural death are either working or are locked up in Goodwood Prison.
Yet months later, nobody has been charged with any crime.

(VO15) UNTIL NOW, FORTUIN’S MOTHER HAD SEEN GOODWOOD CORRECTIONAL FACILITY ALMOST AS HER SON’S SECOND HOME - A PLACE WHERE HE HAD CELEBRATED SIX BIRTHDAYS AND SPENT MUCH OF HIS ADULT LIFE. SHE BELIEVES HE WAS MURDERED

Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Vir my as sy ma,
For me, as his mother,
om te dink hy’s in die gevangenis,
to think he was in jail,
hy moet veilig wees,
he ought to be safe
en wat gebeur, dat die bewaardes wat na ons kinders moes kyk amper né,
And what happens when the wardens, tasked with looking after our children inside,
om iemand so wreed wreed dood te maak? Pyn en leiding. En hy was gebundu gewees, ja.
kill somebody so violently? Pain and suffering, it was a lynching, yes.

Lourensa Eckard: Maria, hoe ver is jy bereid om te gaan om seker te maak dat diegenes wat vir sy dood verantwoordlik is sal aan die pen draai?
Maria, how far are you willing to go
to ensure those responsible for his death are held accountable?


Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Justice moet geskied word.
Justice must be done.
Ek wil sy - met die moordenaars, ek will hulle sien, ek wil voor hulle sit, en ek wil hulle kyk.
I want to look at the murderers, I want to sit in front of them and look at them.
So ek voel dat dit moet verder gaan.
So I feel we need to take things further.

(VO16) WHILE CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DESCRIBES FORTUIN AS A DANGEROUS REPEAT OFFENDER, HIS LAWYER OF TEN YEARS HOLDS A DIFFERENT VIEW.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
He was not a violent person in prison that I'm aware of, but having known him for that long time, he was very docile, very respectful.

Lourensa Eckard: So you're saying he was a model prisoner.

Labiek Samuels: He was a model prisoner but within the gang system, Quintin was a high-ranking gang member in himself.

National Commissioner: The findings of this investigation point to an urgent need to evaluate the effectiveness of management practices at Goodwood Correctional Center.


(VO17) ON MAY THE FIRST, THE NATIONAL COMMISSIONER MAKGOTHI THOBAKGALE ANNOUNCED THAT CORRECTIONAL SERVICES HAD SUSPENDED FOUR OFFICIALS WHO ARE NOW, WITH OTHERS, FACING DISCIPLINARY HEARINGS.

Lourensa Eckard: Were there any dogs present during this incident?

Singabakho Nxumalo
Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services
The report we have there was one dog and you have seen reports that dogs were let out to attack the offender, which is not true. Yes there was a dog there but at no point you can let the dog bite an offender. No, that's not how we operate.

(VO18) BUT THE CASE HAD ALREADY BEEN ESCALATED TO A BODY CALLED THE JUDICIAL INSPECTORATE OF CORRECTIONAL SERVICES OR JICS FOR AN INVESTIGATION.
WE HAVE HAD SIGHT OF THEIR INTERIM REPORT IN WHICH THEY DESCRIBE THE ATTACK ON FORTUIN AS “BRUTAL”.
IT RECORDS THAT A WITNESS SAW A DOG DRAGGING FORTUIN BY THE LEG.
FURTHER WITNESS ACCOUNTS IN THIS REPORT SAY THAT THE ATTACK ON FORTUIN CONTINUED EVEN AFTER HE WAS DISARMED AND LYING ON THE GROUND.

PTC: There's not a single story of what happened to Quintin Fortuin. There are multiple versions, each with contradictory details - from the prison, the prison watchdog, even the inmates are alleged to have smuggled out a letter with eyewitness accounts of the death of their fellow inmate.

(VO19) SAMUELS SAYS THE LETTER FROM INMATES WAS READ TO HIM OVER THE PHONE.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
This is what the letter contained.They placed him on his knees, and they started beating him. He was then isolated in a single cell, and the emergency response staff, came in and then continued assaulting him. A dog was brought into the cell and set on Quintin. Thereafter, he was taken to what appears to be a courtyard between the cells, and he was further beaten there.

(VO20) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES HAS REJECTED THE ALLEGATIONS MADE BY ANONYMOUS INMATES.

Singabakho Nxumalo
Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services
What we often encounter, inmates who are even four blocks away from the scene will also claim to say, no, we witnessed what happened. We know what happened, when, in fact, they had no clue what happened there. And unfortunately, such reports, at times, will even find its way, you know, to outside parties, even to the media. such wild allegations, no, we’ve not received them.

(VO21) BUT REPORTS OF QUINTIN FORTUIN’S DEATH REACHED DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT, NICHOLAS GOTSELL.
TO SEE FOR HIMSELF, HE ATTEMPTED TO SOURCE CAMERA FOOTAGE OF THE INCIDENT FROM GOODWOOD PRISON.

Nicholas Gotsell
MP, Democratic Alliance
I'm told that the cameras are not functioning. That led me to also ask a lot more questions about other other centers, the answer I got is that most of them are not functioning. … if you have gang problems, drug problems, illicit goods coming in and out and being used in the commission of crimes and fueling the gang and drug problems we have on the Cape Flats, that should be your number one priority that you have cameras that are working.

(VO22) AN ATTORNEY BY TRAINING, GOTSELL HAS BEEN STEADILY BUILDING UP A PROFILE OF WHAT HE CALLS THE “PRISON ECONOMY”.
HE CLAIMS ITS RUN BY SYNDICATES RELYING ON CRIMINALS AND PRISON WARDERS, WITH AWAITING-TRIAL PRISONERS ACTING AS COURIERS WHEN THEY GO TO AND FROM COURT.

Nicholas Gotsell
MP, Democratic Alliance
Our Correctional Services centers are feeding grounds for more crime.

(VO23) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES SAYS ALMOST TWO THOUSAND WEAPONS WERE SMUGGLED INTO GOODWOOD PRISON ALONE LAST YEAR.
FOURTEEN TIK PIPES, 1 and a half kg OF TIK, 175 KG OF DAGGA AND OVER 18-THOUSAND MANDRAX PILLS WERE ALSO SMUGGLED IN TO CAPE PRISONS.
QUINTIN FORTUIN WAS HIGH ON A COCKTAIL OF DRUGS THE NIGHT BEFORE HE DIED.
AND HE HAD A SHARP OBJECT OR WEAPON.

PTC: The glimpses of prison life in South Africa we see through the death of Quintin Fortuin are frightening, where there may well be criminals, at least in some instances, on both sides of the bars.

(VO24) FORTUIN’S LAWYER BELIEVES HIS CLIENT WAS DAYS AWAY FROM BEING ACQUITTED ON MURDER CHARGES, WHEN HE DIED.

Labiek Samuels
Criminal Defence Attorney
I think that if you electrocuted, someone, it would be far less painful than taking a beating like that, which is torturous, but I don't think he deserved to die that way.

(VO25) MARIA FORTUIN SAID HER SON WAS PLANNING TO SETTLE DOWN IN MOSSEL BAY, WITH HER, AFTER HIS RELEASE, TURN OVER A NEW LEAF AND START A FAMILY. THOSE DREAMS ARE NOW BURIED WITH HIS BATTERED BODY IN MAITLAND CEMETERY.

Maria Fortuin
Mother of Quintin Fortuin
Daar’s baie dinge van hom wat ek sal mis.
There are a lot of things I miss about him.
Hy’s een wat gehang af vir my en so gedruk het, en sê Mammie, ek is so lief vir jou.
He would hang on me and hug me tightly
and say, “Mommy, I love you so much.
Ek is so baie lief vir jou.
I love you so very much.”
En skielik, en skielik is net weg.
And suddenly, and suddenly is he just gone.
En alles het kom stil word van hom.
Everything about him is now silent.
Ek sal hom nooit weer sien nie. Hy’s weg vir altyd.
I will never see him again. He’s gone forever.

PROMOS

(VO1) A PRISON INMATE DIES ON A SUNDAY MORNING…
WEARING ONLY UNDERPANTS
AND ON HIS FINGER, A SINGLE RING
LAWYER: I am convinced that his death is a cover up, that the circumstances surrounding his death is a complete cover up.
IT’S A MESSY FIGHT IN A MURKY JAIL.

(VO2)
A BATTERED BODY TELLS A GRUESOME STORY
MOTHER: Sy body wys alles, wat is gemaak met sy body.
His body shows everything that was done to his body.
PHOTOGRAPHS OF A CORPSE PROVIDE CLUES TO AN UNNATURAL DEATH.
LAWYER: I have seen gunshot wounds, I've seen stab wounds, but I've never seen wounds to this extent.

(VO3)
PRISON WARDERS HAMMER A GANGSTER…
YET SAY THEY FOLLOW THE RULES
PRISON SPOKESPERSON: We are not running facilities where officials are at war with offenders, No.
BUT A GRIEVING FAMILY DOESN’T BELIEVE THE STORY THEY HEAR.
MOTHER: Wat die bewaardes gedoen het is erger as wat die gangsters doen.
What the warders did is worse than what the gangsters do.

None of this information squares up to the official version disseminated by the Department of Correctional Services of the death of this notorious inmate who grew up in gang-ridden Delft, and who has been in the crosshairs of the judicial system for his entire adult life. Summary: On the 16th of February, an awaiting trial prisoner at Goodwood Prison failed to emerge immediately out of his cell when called for roll call. According to insiders, he had been doing drugs all night and was slow to react when the other prisoners were called to come outside to kneel down to be counted. He was chivvied by the two warders on duty, who got him to join the tail end of the group. But then an altercation ensued. According to Correctional Services, this prisoner, allegedly a senior general in the 26 gang, produced a home-made sharp object and stabbed a warder. In the scuffle the two warders were injured, one broke his arm, and both are home still recuperating over six weeks later. As for the prisoner, Quinton Fortuin, he ended up naked and fatally injured, and was declared dead in Karl Bremer Hospital four and a half hours later. What happened between about 08h00 in the morning and 11h30 that day when he was declared dead is now contested. It is alleged that Inmate Fortuin was beaten up by wardens who set dogs on him, and then by the EST, the Emergency Security Team that enforces law and order inside the prison walls. It is also alleged that he was dead on the scene and the Department of Correctional Services is desperately trying to cover it up, pretending he died in hospital. They unnatural death - now a criminal investigation into murder - shows how the prison system fails itself, its inmates and the community at large. It raises the problems of understaffing at prisons, the over population of prisons, the lack of humane control, the lack of any type of rehabilitation or leadership and the lack of technological resources. It's been revealed that none of this was captured on camera because the contract to keep the cameras had not been paid in three years, so while the camera could provide images in real time, it could not record. Further information: The story has been in the media, as was the press conference on May the first, but I think there is more to dig in here, than has been reported, and the disconnect between the narratives reveal a serious attempt to cover up the kind of violence which may becoming the norm, in order to keep over crowded, understaffed prisons under control. 2025 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 04 June 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Death Behind Bars In an overcrowded Cape Town prison, an awaiting-trial inmate lies naked, severely beaten. Hours later, he’s declared dead. The official report: the alleged gangster died in a prison fight. But leaked information suggests the story may be far more sinister. What really happened that day? From horrific photos to reports of broken security cameras and attack dogs… whispers swirl, and more questions are raised than answers. Carte Blanche investigates. Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Lourensa Eckard Script: MURDER IN PRISON – the death of Quintin Fortuin Final Script (VO1) IN CAPE TOWN AN AWAITING-TRIAL PRISONER CHARGED WITH MURDER DIES A PAINFUL DEATH…. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney I think the undertaker had gone about three or four times to collect the body. There was always issues with the paperwork. (VO2) THE WOUNDS ON HIS BODY PRESENT EVIDENCE OF A VIOLENT BEATING… Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Hy kom van ‘n moeder af, hy’s sy ma se kind, om iemand so wreed dood te maak, dis nie reg nie. He was born of a mother - he’s his mother’s child. To kill somebody so violently is not right. (VO3) AND THE STORY TOLD BY THE PRISON AUTHORITIES SIMPLY DOESN’T ADD UP. Singabakho Nxumalo Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services Yes, he was disarmed and force was used. Hence, then he needed medical attention. (VO4) 39-YEAR-OLD QUINTIN FORTUIN WAS THE THIRD INMATE TO DIE CONTROVERSIALLY IN SOUTH AFRICAN PRISONS THIS YEAR. THESE DEATHS ARE TEARING OPEN THE VEIL OF SECRECY BEHIND WHICH PRISON OFFICIALS DO THEIR JOBS, ALBEIT UNDER VERY DIFFICULT CIRCUMSTANCES. This is Goodwood Prison in Cape Town. It’s seriously under-staffed - and dangerously over-crowded. On the 16th of February this year, only 95 officials were on duty to manage 2400 prisoners. It was a Sunday morning, and around 08h00 am, we are told, a fight broke out between three warders and a prisoner, a known gangster. (VO5)THE GANGSTER WAS QUINTIN “QUESTION” FORTUIN A HIGH-RANKING MEMBER OF A PRISON GANG…A GENERAL IN THE 26S. HE REPORTEDLY REFUSED TO COME OUT FROM HIS CELL TO BE COUNTED AND THEN, WE ARE TOLD, UNPROVOKED, HE STABBED A WARDER. (VO6) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES SPOKESPERSON SINGABAKHO NXUMALO SAID THREE OFFICIALS BATTLED TO RESTRAIN THE INMATE WHO WEIGHED ONLY 60 KG. Singabakho Nxumalo Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services The official was badly stabbed. In trying to defend himself, he even fell and broke his arm. Another official tried also to assist. He also got injured. Other officials realized that we needed more manpower here, and then, I think they managed then to defuse the situation. But in that act, force was used. The incident happened at about 10 past eight in the morning. He was then taken to Karl Bremer hospital and he passed on just after twelve midday. That is when we received a call that he had passed on. It takes about fifteen minutes to drive from Goodwood Prison to Karl Bremer Hospital within the speed limit, on a Sunday. The post mortem says Quintin Fortuin was delivered to the hospital just before 11h00 am. So what happened in the hours before that? (VO7) THE PRISONS SPOKESPERSON SAYS THE SITUATION WAS TOO “DYNAMIC” TO PROVIDE A DETAILED TIME-BOUND BREAKDOWN OF THE SEQUENCE OF EVENTS. Singabakho Nxumalo: It's not just a matter of saying that you slapped me, I slapped you, and that's the end of the story. Lourensa Eckard: Well, we have a body. Singabakho Nxumalo: Yes. Lourensa Eckard: Someone died. Siyabakho Nxumalo: Yes, and there is a number of people in that particular space. Let's allow that process to take time, otherwise it will not do us any good in saying, let's rush, rush. (VO7b)BUT FORTUIN’S LAWYER, LABIEK SAMUELS, WANTED TO FIND OUT. AFTER MAKING OVER A HUNDRED PHONE CALLS TO THE PRISON, HE LOCATED HIS CLIENT AT A MORTUARY. AND ACCOMPANIED HIS MOTHER TO IDENTIFY HER SON, THROUGH A SMALL WINDOW. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney When we came to the mortuary, the body was placed in such a position that one could not see any of the injuries sustained.ut you could see that his jaw was dislocated and his eyes were still open. His mother then entered the room, and she collapsed. (VO8) FORTUIN’S MOTHER, MARIA, IS STILL IN A STATE OF DISBELIEF. Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Hy’t gelê daar. He lay there; Sy mond was wa-wyd oop. his mouth was wide open, Sy kop was so effens oop, en krappe in sy gesig. his eye was slightly open, and he had scratches on his face. (VO9) BUT MARIA SAYS THAT AT THE MORTUARY SHE SUSPECTED THERE WAS MORE TO HER SON’S DEATH THAN MET THE EYE: HE WAS NAKED EXCEPT FOR BOXER SHORTS AND THIS PIECE OF JEWELLERY. Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Wat ek gekry daar was net ‘n ring. What I got there was only a ring. En ‘n trunkie, dis al. and boxer shorts - that’s all. Verder, het ons niks verder gekry nie, Toe vra ek die outjie wat daar werk: So ek vra waar’s die klere? We received nothing further. It was all that he had on him. So, I asked the guy who worked there, “Where are his clothes?” Hy sê nee hy kom van Karl Bremer af net met ‘n trunkie aan. He said, no, he came from Karl Bremer Hospital in only his underwear. (VO10) SO THEY TRACKED BACK TO KARL BREMER HOSPITAL TO FIND HIS CLOTHES AND HOPEFULLY MORE CLUES. Labiek Samuels: We were also told that he arrived there in that state. Now this exacerbated the entire scenario. Lourensa Eckard: Did you get the idea that the Correctional Service officials - that they were not completely forthcoming about what had happened? Labiek Samuels: Most definitely, the version that we were told did not make sense. (VO11) AT THE TIME, GOODWOOD PRISON TOLD THEM FORTUIN HAD NO POSSESSIONS. AND THEY OFFERED TO BURY THE BODY THEMSELVES, A CLAIM WHICH CORRECTIONAL SERVICES NOW SAYS IS STRANGE. Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Hulle wil nie die body van my kind release nie. They didn’t want to release the body of my child. Die Vrydag moet die prokureur weer foon vir iemand om te sê release Quintin Fortuin se body en tog release hulle die body vir ons. That Friday, the lawyer had to phone someone again to say they must release Quintin Fortuin’s body. And only then did they release him to us. (VO12)HIS BLOODIED BODY WAS FINALLY PREPARED FOR BURIAL BY UNDERTAKER, JP DAVIDS. JP Davids Undertaker Met Quintin jy kon sien daar’s taamlike ‘’n bietjie plekke wat waar hy’t baie seer gekry het. With Quintin, you could see there were quite a few places where he was very badly hurt. (VO13) DAVIDS HELPED SAMUELS PHOTOGRAPH THE DEAD MAN’S WOUNDS. FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE LAWYER SAW BOTH SIDES OF THE CORPSE. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney I saw lacerations of his body. I saw bruises. I saw broken wrist. I saw dog bites and I saw stab wounds. JP Davids Undertaker Daar was natuurlik byt-merke op hom, dit kan ek honderd per sent sê. There were, of course, also bite marks on him, that I can say for sure Ons het diep snye op hom gekry en so on, so ja. We also found deep cuts on his him and so on. (VO14) DOG BITE MARKS WERE NOT RECORDED ON THE POST MORTEM REPORT. NOT ALL THE WOUNDS IN THE PHOTOS WERE ACCOUNTED FOR IN THE VERSION OF EVENTS PROVIDED BY THE PRISON. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney There was no sign for me that there was any medical intervention, and that, raised more questions. And from there, I contacted the detective. PTC: The police are pursuing a charge of murder into the death of Quintin Fortuin. The eyewitnesses to his unnatural death are either working or are locked up in Goodwood Prison. Yet months later, nobody has been charged with any crime. (VO15) UNTIL NOW, FORTUIN’S MOTHER HAD SEEN GOODWOOD CORRECTIONAL FACILITY ALMOST AS HER SON’S SECOND HOME - A PLACE WHERE HE HAD CELEBRATED SIX BIRTHDAYS AND SPENT MUCH OF HIS ADULT LIFE. SHE BELIEVES HE WAS MURDERED Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Vir my as sy ma, For me, as his mother, om te dink hy’s in die gevangenis, to think he was in jail, hy moet veilig wees, he ought to be safe en wat gebeur, dat die bewaardes wat na ons kinders moes kyk amper né, And what happens when the wardens, tasked with looking after our children inside, om iemand so wreed wreed dood te maak? Pyn en leiding. En hy was gebundu gewees, ja. kill somebody so violently? Pain and suffering, it was a lynching, yes. Lourensa Eckard: Maria, hoe ver is jy bereid om te gaan om seker te maak dat diegenes wat vir sy dood verantwoordlik is sal aan die pen draai? Maria, how far are you willing to go to ensure those responsible for his death are held accountable? Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Justice moet geskied word. Justice must be done. Ek wil sy - met die moordenaars, ek will hulle sien, ek wil voor hulle sit, en ek wil hulle kyk. I want to look at the murderers, I want to sit in front of them and look at them. So ek voel dat dit moet verder gaan. So I feel we need to take things further. (VO16) WHILE CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DESCRIBES FORTUIN AS A DANGEROUS REPEAT OFFENDER, HIS LAWYER OF TEN YEARS HOLDS A DIFFERENT VIEW. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney He was not a violent person in prison that I'm aware of, but having known him for that long time, he was very docile, very respectful. Lourensa Eckard: So you're saying he was a model prisoner. Labiek Samuels: He was a model prisoner but within the gang system, Quintin was a high-ranking gang member in himself. National Commissioner: The findings of this investigation point to an urgent need to evaluate the effectiveness of management practices at Goodwood Correctional Center. (VO17) ON MAY THE FIRST, THE NATIONAL COMMISSIONER MAKGOTHI THOBAKGALE ANNOUNCED THAT CORRECTIONAL SERVICES HAD SUSPENDED FOUR OFFICIALS WHO ARE NOW, WITH OTHERS, FACING DISCIPLINARY HEARINGS. Lourensa Eckard: Were there any dogs present during this incident? Singabakho Nxumalo Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services The report we have there was one dog and you have seen reports that dogs were let out to attack the offender, which is not true. Yes there was a dog there but at no point you can let the dog bite an offender. No, that's not how we operate. (VO18) BUT THE CASE HAD ALREADY BEEN ESCALATED TO A BODY CALLED THE JUDICIAL INSPECTORATE OF CORRECTIONAL SERVICES OR JICS FOR AN INVESTIGATION. WE HAVE HAD SIGHT OF THEIR INTERIM REPORT IN WHICH THEY DESCRIBE THE ATTACK ON FORTUIN AS “BRUTAL”. IT RECORDS THAT A WITNESS SAW A DOG DRAGGING FORTUIN BY THE LEG. FURTHER WITNESS ACCOUNTS IN THIS REPORT SAY THAT THE ATTACK ON FORTUIN CONTINUED EVEN AFTER HE WAS DISARMED AND LYING ON THE GROUND. PTC: There's not a single story of what happened to Quintin Fortuin. There are multiple versions, each with contradictory details - from the prison, the prison watchdog, even the inmates are alleged to have smuggled out a letter with eyewitness accounts of the death of their fellow inmate. (VO19) SAMUELS SAYS THE LETTER FROM INMATES WAS READ TO HIM OVER THE PHONE. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney This is what the letter contained.They placed him on his knees, and they started beating him. He was then isolated in a single cell, and the emergency response staff, came in and then continued assaulting him. A dog was brought into the cell and set on Quintin. Thereafter, he was taken to what appears to be a courtyard between the cells, and he was further beaten there. (VO20) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES HAS REJECTED THE ALLEGATIONS MADE BY ANONYMOUS INMATES. Singabakho Nxumalo Spokesperson, Department of Correctional Services What we often encounter, inmates who are even four blocks away from the scene will also claim to say, no, we witnessed what happened. We know what happened, when, in fact, they had no clue what happened there. And unfortunately, such reports, at times, will even find its way, you know, to outside parties, even to the media. such wild allegations, no, we’ve not received them. (VO21) BUT REPORTS OF QUINTIN FORTUIN’S DEATH REACHED DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT, NICHOLAS GOTSELL. TO SEE FOR HIMSELF, HE ATTEMPTED TO SOURCE CAMERA FOOTAGE OF THE INCIDENT FROM GOODWOOD PRISON. Nicholas Gotsell MP, Democratic Alliance I'm told that the cameras are not functioning. That led me to also ask a lot more questions about other other centers, the answer I got is that most of them are not functioning. … if you have gang problems, drug problems, illicit goods coming in and out and being used in the commission of crimes and fueling the gang and drug problems we have on the Cape Flats, that should be your number one priority that you have cameras that are working. (VO22) AN ATTORNEY BY TRAINING, GOTSELL HAS BEEN STEADILY BUILDING UP A PROFILE OF WHAT HE CALLS THE “PRISON ECONOMY”. HE CLAIMS ITS RUN BY SYNDICATES RELYING ON CRIMINALS AND PRISON WARDERS, WITH AWAITING-TRIAL PRISONERS ACTING AS COURIERS WHEN THEY GO TO AND FROM COURT. Nicholas Gotsell MP, Democratic Alliance Our Correctional Services centers are feeding grounds for more crime. (VO23) CORRECTIONAL SERVICES SAYS ALMOST TWO THOUSAND WEAPONS WERE SMUGGLED INTO GOODWOOD PRISON ALONE LAST YEAR. FOURTEEN TIK PIPES, 1 and a half kg OF TIK, 175 KG OF DAGGA AND OVER 18-THOUSAND MANDRAX PILLS WERE ALSO SMUGGLED IN TO CAPE PRISONS. QUINTIN FORTUIN WAS HIGH ON A COCKTAIL OF DRUGS THE NIGHT BEFORE HE DIED. AND HE HAD A SHARP OBJECT OR WEAPON. PTC: The glimpses of prison life in South Africa we see through the death of Quintin Fortuin are frightening, where there may well be criminals, at least in some instances, on both sides of the bars. (VO24) FORTUIN’S LAWYER BELIEVES HIS CLIENT WAS DAYS AWAY FROM BEING ACQUITTED ON MURDER CHARGES, WHEN HE DIED. Labiek Samuels Criminal Defence Attorney I think that if you electrocuted, someone, it would be far less painful than taking a beating like that, which is torturous, but I don't think he deserved to die that way. (VO25) MARIA FORTUIN SAID HER SON WAS PLANNING TO SETTLE DOWN IN MOSSEL BAY, WITH HER, AFTER HIS RELEASE, TURN OVER A NEW LEAF AND START A FAMILY. THOSE DREAMS ARE NOW BURIED WITH HIS BATTERED BODY IN MAITLAND CEMETERY. Maria Fortuin Mother of Quintin Fortuin Daar’s baie dinge van hom wat ek sal mis. There are a lot of things I miss about him. Hy’s een wat gehang af vir my en so gedruk het, en sê Mammie, ek is so lief vir jou. He would hang on me and hug me tightly and say, “Mommy, I love you so much. Ek is so baie lief vir jou. I love you so very much.” En skielik, en skielik is net weg. And suddenly, and suddenly is he just gone. En alles het kom stil word van hom. Everything about him is now silent. Ek sal hom nooit weer sien nie. Hy’s weg vir altyd. I will never see him again. He’s gone forever. PROMOS (VO1) A PRISON INMATE DIES ON A SUNDAY MORNING… WEARING ONLY UNDERPANTS AND ON HIS FINGER, A SINGLE RING LAWYER: I am convinced that his death is a cover up, that the circumstances surrounding his death is a complete cover up. IT’S A MESSY FIGHT IN A MURKY JAIL. (VO2) A BATTERED BODY TELLS A GRUESOME STORY MOTHER: Sy body wys alles, wat is gemaak met sy body. His body shows everything that was done to his body. PHOTOGRAPHS OF A CORPSE PROVIDE CLUES TO AN UNNATURAL DEATH. LAWYER: I have seen gunshot wounds, I've seen stab wounds, but I've never seen wounds to this extent. (VO3) PRISON WARDERS HAMMER A GANGSTER… YET SAY THEY FOLLOW THE RULES PRISON SPOKESPERSON: We are not running facilities where officials are at war with offenders, No. BUT A GRIEVING FAMILY DOESN’T BELIEVE THE STORY THEY HEAR. MOTHER: Wat die bewaardes gedoen het is erger as wat die gangsters doen. What the warders did is worse than what the gangsters do.
